claims.label: Wilson Opened Debate by Reading From His Phone About "Never-Before-Seen Messages," Per Clip Host Plays
claims.claim: The host plays a clip in which Andrew Wilson, reading from his phone, opens the debate by saying he holds "never before seen messages" from Charlie Kirk to his security team dated September 9, 2025.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify whether Wilson subsequently publishes the underlying message text and cross-reference its platform of origin (Signal vs. iMessage) against prior Owens claims and Erika Kirk's prior December 2025 Glenn Beck statements.

claims.label: Wilson Stated 75–85% Likelihood That Tyler Robinson Killed Charlie Kirk
claims.claim: When asked by the moderator for a 0–100 estimate of the likelihood that Tyler Robinson shot and killed Charlie Kirk, Andrew Wilson answered 75–85%.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Wilson's stated confidence level against his debate claim that the evidence against Robinson is "overwhelming."

claims.label: Wilson Could Not Name Any of the Seven Charges Against Tyler Robinson
claims.claim: When challenged during the debate to name any of the seven charges Tyler Robinson faces, Andrew Wilson could not do so and ultimately named a charge (murder) that Owens stated was not on the list.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference the published charging instrument from the Utah case to verify the seven-count list and confirm which charge(s) Wilson named correctly versus incorrectly.

claims.label: Host Says Wilson Repeatedly Used the Phrase "Positive Evidence" During the Debate
claims.claim: The host says that in the next phase of the debate Andrew Wilson kept saying the phrase "positive evidence", which she says seemed like a term he had just learned and wanted to use.
claims.investigative_direction: Count exact repetitions in full debate transcript; this claim is repeated in internet memes (A-2279.1) which may be cross-referenced for the specific count (the meme states 47).

claims.label: Patrick Bet-David (PBD) Moderated the Debate
claims.claim: The discussion between Candace Owens and Andrew Wilson was moderated by Patrick Bet-David (PBD).
claims.investigative_direction: Verify PBD's role through the published debate recording on his platform; confirm two named team members (Tom and PBD's executive assistant) were present on the pre-debate FaceTime call.

claims.label: Steven Crowder Was on the Phone With Andrew Wilson Immediately After the Debate
claims.claim: Immediately after the debate concluded, Steven Crowder telephoned Andrew Wilson and asked whether Wilson had been provided hair and makeup services, to which Wilson replied he would have refused them.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify any further post-debate coordination between Crowder's organization and Wilson; verify whether the hair/makeup assertion contradicts the published terms of the debate.

claims.label: Host Says Poly Market Odds on Tyler Robinson Conviction Dropped During the Debate
claims.claim: The host says the Poly Market prediction market odds on a Tyler Robinson conviction fell during the debate, and she thinks they hit approximately 34% mid-debate.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the full Poly Market time series for the relevant market to confirm the percentage trajectory during the debate window.

claims.label: Rachel Wilson Publicly Acknowledged That Owens Knew the Case Details Better
claims.claim: Rachel Wilson posted on X stating, in effect, that Candace Owens would naturally know the case details better than Andrew Wilson, citing Wilson's approximately six days of preparation.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the full text of Rachel Wilson's X post to confirm the exact wording and timestamp.

claims.label: Rachel Wilson Publicly Suggested the In-Ear Monitors May Have Been Used to Feed Owens Answers
claims.claim: The host says Rachel Wilson, replying to a post asking whether the host was being fed answers through her in-ear monitor, wrote that she knew they had headpieces but was not sure why they had them, and believed the contract allowed each to wear an earpiece.
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the full text of Rachel Wilson's X post; verify against published debate technical setup, including Candace Owens's claim that the earpieces had a 15-foot operational range and could not extend outside the control room.

claims.label: Wilson Retweeted Comment About Tyler Robinson Defense and Replied "Picked a hell of a week"
claims.claim: Prior to the debate, Andrew Wilson retweeted a comment reading "skimmed it. The Tyler Robinson dispense defense is on absolute life support" and added the reply "Picked a hell of a week."
claims.investigative_direction: Retrieve the full X post with timestamp; identify the original poster; cross-reference with the dismissal filing released two days before the debate.

claims.label: "Jars Wide Shut" AI Video by @whereforbidden Was Created Reacting to the Debate
claims.claim: An AI-generated video titled "Jars Wide Shut," depicting Erika Kirk confronting Andrew Wilson, was created by the X account @whereforbidden and circulated as a post-debate reaction.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify original posting timestamp; verify whether @whereforbidden's content has prior documented activity in the series.

claims.label: "Stages of Debate Grief" Meme by @alpha_approved Was Created Reacting to the Debate
claims.claim: The host reads a post from the X account @alpha_approved listing "five stages of debate grief" for Andrew Wilson, from denial ("I totally won that debate") to acceptance, as a reaction to the debate.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify original posting timestamp; verify whether @alpha_approved's content has prior documented activity in the series.

claims.label: In Clip Host Plays, Wilson's Opening Statement Included "I Have His Cell Phone"
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Erika Kirk says she and Charlie Kirk promised each other never to live in fear, that he was not messaging people the day before saying he would be murdered, and "And I have his cell phone."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify whether the cell phone referenced matches the device referenced in prior Erika Kirk statements and the September 9, 2025 message provenance question (N-10794).

claims.label: Host says TPUSA brought Wilson in to train its students to debate
claims.claim: The host says Turning Point USA brought Andrew Wilson in to train its students how to debate and paid him to do so.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain TPUSA event schedules, invoices or student-chapter communications showing a Wilson debate-training engagement and any payment.
claims.transcript_snippet: they brought that guy in to train Turning Point USA students how to debate.

claims.label: Host says Charlie Kirk trained her to debate on campus trips
claims.claim: The host says she was trained to debate by Charlie Kirk, over many hours of note-card practice while traveling to college campuses.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate dated campus-tour footage or staff accounts of Kirk coaching the host on debate technique.
claims.transcript_snippet: I was trained to debate by Charlie Kirk cross country across too many college campuses.

claims.label: Host says Wilson visited TPUSA headquarters in June and afterwards began challenging her
claims.claim: The host says Andrew Wilson went into TPUSA headquarters in June and came out acting as though he were a billionaire dropping her name. (At 00:32:30 she places the visit in May; see flags.)
claims.investigative_direction: Establish the date(s) of any Wilson visit to TPUSA headquarters (visitor logs, Wilson's own posts, TPUSA staff statements) and the timing of his first public challenge to the host.
claims.transcript_snippet: Goes into TPUSA headquarters in June. Comes out and suddenly he thinks that I don't know.

claims.label: Host says Wilson insisted on negotiating the debate terms publicly on X
claims.claim: The host says Andrew Wilson demanded that the debate terms be negotiated publicly on X rather than by email, and refused to email until the format (a minimum of three and a half hours) was agreed, which took about a day and a half.
claims.investigative_direction: Review the public X exchange between Wilson and the host for the negotiation dates and terms.
claims.transcript_snippet: Andrew Wilson demanded that I publicly negotiate the terms of the agreement on X.

claims.label: Host says she agreed to Wilson's video guy, fact checkers and moderator choice
claims.claim: The host says her side agreed that Wilson could bring a video person and his own fact checkers (a party of four) and pick the moderator, conceding almost every point.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the publicly posted terms and the signed contract against the party that actually arrived.
claims.transcript_snippet: We also agreed, as you saw publicly, that he could bring his own fact checkers. Essentially, he's coming with a party of four.

claims.label: Host says Wilson's side emailed through an unnamed 'Crucible team'
claims.claim: The host says her side received no names for the people on Wilson's email chain, who identified themselves only as the 'Crucible team', even though her side had listed all of its own names.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the email chain headers and signature blocks to see who sent from the 'Crucible team' address.
claims.transcript_snippet: I am provided with no identity as to who I am communicating with.

claims.label: Host says the Crucible team demanded a contract and an escrow account
claims.claim: The host says the Crucible team asked for a contract and an escrow account for the funds, accepted her lawyer's account as the escrow, and her lawyer drafted a contract reflecting the publicly agreed terms.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the draft and signed contract and any escrow correspondence between the two sides' lawyers.
claims.transcript_snippet: they then declare that they would like a contract and an escrow account for the funds.

claims.label: Host says the Crucible team tried to void terms after a Joe Rogan hosting offer
claims.claim: The host says the Crucible team emailed that Joe Rogan had made an offer to host the discussion in Texas, wrote that this 'changes everything', and proposed blowing up the negotiated terms.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the email and ask Rogan's team whether and when an offer to host was made.
claims.transcript_snippet: Joe Rogan has now made an offer to host this discussion down in Texas.

claims.label: Host says Wilson's side offered a luxury car to bring her to Texas
claims.claim: The host says the Crucible team offered her a luxury car to accommodate her pregnancy for the trip to Texas, and she declined, holding to her conditions of no travel and no smoking.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the email containing the car offer and the host's reply.
claims.transcript_snippet: They offer me a luxury car to accommodate my pregnancy and I say no.

claims.label: Host says Michael Knowles declined to moderate, so Wilson asked PBD
claims.claim: The host says Michael Knowles told Wilson he would not moderate, and Wilson then called Patrick Bet-David and asked him to moderate.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask Bet-David's and Knowles' offices when Knowles declined and when Bet-David was approached.
claims.transcript_snippet: Andrew then calls PBD and asks him to moderate because Michael Knowles said that he wasn't going to moderate.

claims.label: Host says the Crucible team demanded a guaranteed 90-minute question session
claims.claim: The host says the Crucible team tried to renegotiate agreed terms to give Wilson a guaranteed 90 minutes in which to question her, which she compares to a deposition, and that she refused.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the renegotiation email and the final contract text on question periods.
claims.transcript_snippet: they want to have a guaranteed 90 minutes to basically sit me through a deposition where he can just go at me and ask me questions

claims.label: Host says Wilson dropped the deposition demand on a Tuesday FaceTime with PBD
claims.claim: The host says that on a Tuesday-evening FaceTime call with Bet-David present, Wilson changed tone and said he did not need to ask her questions or add that to the contract.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask Bet-David's team (the host names Tom and an executive assistant on the call) to confirm what was agreed on the call.
claims.transcript_snippet: Oh, yeah, no, it's fine. I don't need to, you know, ask her questions or do anything like that or add that to the contract.

claims.label: Host says she explained her studio limits and the allowed monitoring arrangements
claims.claim: The host says she told Wilson's side that filming was allowed only inside her small studio because her children live and homeschool in the house, and offered a control-room listening spot for his team.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the contract's filming clause with the host's account of the FaceTime call.
claims.transcript_snippet: we are not allowing them to film anywhere but inside of this exact studio.

claims.label: Host says the contract was officially signed on Thursday
claims.claim: The host says the debate contract was officially signed on the Thursday before the Friday debate.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the signed contract with signature dates.
claims.transcript_snippet: contract gets officially signed on Thursday.

claims.label: Host says the contact number given for Wilson's team appeared to be a burner phone
claims.claim: The host says that after her producer asked Bet-David's team for a contact for Wilson, the number supplied appeared to be a burner phone whose user would not identify themselves.
claims.investigative_direction: Have the producer preserve the text thread and number lookup results.
claims.transcript_snippet: It appears to be a burner phone.

claims.label: Host says an anonymous contact demanded a desk, HDMI cable and power for a live stream in her home
claims.claim: The host says the night before the debate the anonymous contact told her producer they would need a desk, an HDMI cable running from the studio to the control room, and power to set up a live stream for Wilson, and said they thought this was implied by the contract's live-stream wording.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the text thread and the contract's live-stream clause.
claims.transcript_snippet: they're going to need a desk. They're going to need a place to set up Andrew's live stream.

claims.label: Host says the live-stream request emails came at 9:15 p.m. and 11:15 p.m. the night before
claims.claim: The host says Wilson's side emailed about the live-stream assumption at 9:15 p.m. the night before the debate, with a follow-up at 11:15 p.m., and never named the four people it was bringing.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the two emails with timestamps.
claims.transcript_snippet: 9:15 PM the night before the debate with a follow-up email sent at 11:15 p. m.

claims.label: Host says Wilson arrived with Steven Crowder's team including Gerald Morgan
claims.claim: The host says Wilson turned up with Steven Crowder's team, naming Gerald Morgan as the person Wilson brought, and that this explained the secrecy.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the identities of the four-person party with Crowder's company and the debate's security or visitor list.
claims.transcript_snippet: he shows up with Steven Crowder's team.

claims.label: Host says Wilson's party was made to enter through the basement door
claims.claim: The host says her side had Wilson's party enter through the back basement door instead of the front door she normally uses for guests.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask the host's staff or Wilson's party to confirm the entrance used.
claims.transcript_snippet: they had to go through the back through the basement door

claims.label: Host says Gerald did a live call-in from her children's playroom outside the studio
claims.claim: The host says Gerald decided to do a live call-in from her children's playroom just outside the studio, despite her explaining that filming was limited to the studio.
claims.investigative_direction: Check Crowder's channel for any live call-in on debate day and its time.
claims.transcript_snippet: Gerald decided to do a live callin from my kids' playroom just outside the studio.

claims.label: Host alleges Crowder's brand fell after he was caught berating his pregnant wife on a doorbell camera
claims.claim: The host says Steven Crowder's brand "sort of crashed and burned" when he was caught on a doorbell cam berating his eight-month pregnant now ex-wife, who was pregnant with twins, and that he never really recovered from that.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate contemporaneous reporting and the footage the host refers to.
claims.transcript_snippet: when he was caught on a doorbell cam berating his eight-month pregnant now ex-wife when she was pregnant with twins.

claims.label: Host says the contract stipulated no filming outside the studio
claims.claim: The host says one term of the contract stipulated no filming outside the studio, and that the live call-in violated it.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the contract and read the filming clause.
claims.transcript_snippet: one thing the contract did stipulate was no filming outside of this studio.

claims.label: Host says she is moving out of the house in a couple of weeks
claims.claim: The host says she is knowingly moving out of the house where the debate took place in a couple of weeks.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the move through later episodes or host statements.
claims.transcript_snippet: knowingly moving out of this house in a couple of weeks or so

claims.label: Host says she wanted TPUSA to claim Wilson as its own but he refused
claims.claim: The host says one of her proposed terms was that Turning Point USA publicly claim Wilson as its guy, and that Wilson refused and said he had nothing to do with the organization.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the public negotiation posts on this term and any TPUSA statement on Wilson.
claims.transcript_snippet: I wanted turning point to claim their horse. I wanted them to say that this is our guy and he said he didn't want that done.

claims.label: Host says Wilson's opening showed TPUSA was backing him
claims.claim: The host says that within the first three minutes of the debate, Wilson made clear that TPUSA was backing him by citing a never-before-seen message, which she says makes Erika Kirk look like a liar.
claims.investigative_direction: Establish how Wilson obtained the message and whether TPUSA or Erika Kirk supplied it.
claims.transcript_snippet: in the first three minutes of the debate, he makes it perfectly clear that Turning Point USA is backing him

claims.label: Played message: Charlie Kirk told his security team to protect only one person because he feared the left
claims.claim: In the message Wilson read aloud, Charlie Kirk replies to his security team, 'remind them that they are there for one person's security only because I'm somewhat worried the left is trying to kill me', in a message dated September 9, 2025.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original message with metadata and the security team's message it replied to.
claims.transcript_snippet: remind them that they are there for one person's security only because I'm somewhat worried the left is trying to kill me.

claims.label: Played message: security team said campus police and its own team would cover the event, with 11 on site
claims.claim: In the message Wilson read, Charlie Kirk's security team wrote that law enforcement was supportive, that the next day's event would be covered by its team and campus police, with patrol units available and 11 on site.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare the stated '11 on site' with UVU and TPUSA security staffing records for September 10, 2025.
claims.transcript_snippet: Tomorrow's event will be covered by both my team and the campus PD.

claims.label: Played clip: a speaker says Charlie never messaged that he would be murdered and 'I have his cell phone'
claims.claim: In a clip played just after Wilson's reading, a speaker says Charlie and she promised never to live in fear, that he was not messaging people the day before saying he would be murdered, and 'I have his cell phone'. The host goes on to tie this to Erika Kirk's mid-December Glenn Beck appearance, which indicates the speaker is Erika Kirk rather than Wilson.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the clip's source (the December 2025 Glenn Beck interview or the debate's played clips) and confirm the speaker.
claims.transcript_snippet: He didn't. He didn't say that. And I have his cell phone.

claims.label: Host says Erika Kirk came to Nashville for a summit days after the Glenn Beck interview
claims.claim: The host says that days after Erika Kirk's mid-December Glenn Beck appearance, Erika came to Nashville and they held a summit.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the date of the Nashville meeting from travel records or both parties' statements.
claims.transcript_snippet: days after that is when Erika then came to Nashville and we had this summit

claims.label: Host says Erika told her the message was on Signal and auto-deleted
claims.claim: The host says that at the Nashville meeting Erika Kirk told her the message was on Signal and that the team's Signal messages auto-delete, and that Erika did not know because, the host guesses, Dan Flood had not told her.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask TPUSA and Erika Kirk which app carried the message and whether Signal disappearing-message settings were enabled.
claims.transcript_snippet: it was on Signal and the team's messages autodelete on Signal and she didn't know.

claims.label: Host says the message was actually sent by iMessage, not Signal
claims.claim: The host says the message was actually sent by iMessage, that she told viewers Erika lied twice, and that she knows for a fact it was iMessage.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the message with its originating-app metadata (iMessage versus Signal).
claims.transcript_snippet: The message was actually sent on iMessage.

claims.label: Host says TPUSA claims Erika was not told for four months while the host was told in September
claims.claim: The host says the TPUSA side expects people to believe Erika was not told of the message for four months, although the host says someone told her about it in September.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify who told the host in September and when Erika Kirk learned of the message.
claims.transcript_snippet: supposed to believe you didn't tell her for four months, but you told me in September

claims.label: Host says Wilson promised to release the message on his show
claims.claim: The host says Wilson has promised to release the message on his show as evidence, and that she knows it was sent by iMessage although he describes it as Signal.
claims.investigative_direction: Check Wilson's show after August 17, 2026 for the release and the message's metadata.
claims.transcript_snippet: Andrew, who has promised that he's going to release this on his show cuz he's got evidence, actually does release that message

claims.label: Host says Wilson wrongly claimed she said 'girl boss'
claims.claim: In a played exchange, Wilson tells the host the term 'girl boss' came out of her mouth. The host says he raised it himself and that she never said it, and that he repeatedly asserted such false claims about the debate.
claims.investigative_direction: Check the debate transcript for who first said 'girl boss'.
claims.transcript_snippet: He literally came out of his mouth. I never said girl boss.

claims.label: Host says Wilson shifted position to supporting Erika Kirk as CEO
claims.claim: The host says she asked Wilson to explain how he shifted his position and now supports Erika Kirk being a CEO.
claims.investigative_direction: Find Wilson's earlier posts on women leading organizations and compare with his debate statements.
claims.transcript_snippet: how he shifted his position on now he suddenly supports Erika being a CEO

claims.label: Host says Utah's 1102 rule allows hearsay at the preliminary hearing stage
claims.claim: The host says the preliminary hearing repeatedly discussed Utah's Rule 1102, under which hearsay is allowed at that stage as probative, and that this lets people infer from the evidence outside the courtroom too.
claims.investigative_direction: Read Utah Rule of Evidence 1102 and the preliminary-hearing rulings applying it.
claims.transcript_snippet: yeah, we allow this at this stage, it's probitative

claims.label: Host says she reported the Foreign Legion threat to officials and gave it to Tulsi Gabbard's office
claims.claim: In a played exchange, the host says she reported the claimed Foreign Legion threat to the correct government officials and handed the information to Tulsi Gabbard's office.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask Gabbard's office whether it received such information and when.
claims.transcript_snippet: I handed over that information to Tulsi Gabbard's office.

claims.label: Host says in the clip that she cannot say for certainty that Israel called the shots
claims.claim: In a played exchange, the host says that we cannot say for certainty that Israel called the shots and this is how it happened, but that it is definitively, she thinks, a threat that a lot of people would like to see.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare with the host's earlier statements on Israeli involvement to see whether the framing is consistent.
